33.commentaire: The gathering of the entire city at Jesus' door reminds us of the importance of seeking the Lord together. As a community of believers, we are called to come together to worship, pray, and learn from His word. This encourages us to be active witnesses of Christ's power in our lives and to invite others to join us in this spiritual quest.

mots.sens: This verb means 'to heal' and is often used in the New Testament to describe Jesus' action of restoring physical and spiritual health. It evokes not only physical healing but also a complete restoration of the person. In this verse, it emphasizes Jesus' authority over diseases and His role as the Healer of souls.

This term refers to a 'demon' or an evil spirit. In Jewish and Greco-Roman culture, demons were often perceived as entities that could negatively influence humans. The mention of Jesus casting out demons highlights His power over the forces of evil and His mission of liberation for those who are oppressed.

This verb means 'to permit' or 'to allow.' In the context of this verse, it indicates that Jesus has total control over what happens around Him, including the demons that recognize Him. This underscores His divine authority and His ability to restrain evil forces.

34.epoque: This passage is set at the beginning of Jesus' ministry, in a context where Jewish beliefs about healing and exorcism were deeply rooted. Jesus' miracles were signs of the coming of the Kingdom of God and the power of the Holy Spirit.
34.passage: In Mark 1, Jesus begins His public ministry by preaching and healing. This verse illustrates His authority and compassion, showing how He responds to the physical and spiritual needs of the people around Him.
34.culture: In Jesus' time, illness and demonic possession were often seen as manifestations of sin or curse. Healers and exorcists were common, but Jesus stands out for His unique authority and ability to heal instantly.
34.interpretation: This verse reveals that Jesus is not only a healer but also a liberator. The demons recognizing His authority highlight His divine nature and His role as Savior. This reminds us that Jesus has the power to free us from all forms of oppression, whether physical or spiritual.
34.commentaire: This passage encourages us to recognize Jesus' authority in our lives. Just as He healed and liberated those in need, He is always ready to intervene in our struggles. By placing our faith in Him, we can experience His healing and deliverance power today.

mots.sens: This word means 'prayer' and comes from the root 'ευχή' (euché) which evokes a vow or supplication. In the context of Mark 1:35, it emphasizes the importance of communication with God, particularly in moments of solitude. Prayer is an act of dependence and seeking divine will, essential for the spiritual life of the believer.

This term translates to 'desert' and refers to an isolated place, often associated with solitude and meeting with God. In the Bible, the desert is a space where one withdraws to focus on prayer and meditation. It also evokes the idea of purification and spiritual preparation, as in the case of Jesus who withdraws to recharge before continuing His ministry.

This word means 'sign' or 'miracle,' and it is often used to refer to the powerful acts of God that attest to His presence and authority. In the context of Mark, Jesus' miracles are manifestations of His divine identity. This reminds us that prayer and seeking God prepare the ground to see signs of His power in our lives.

35.epoque: The account is set in the 1st century, during the earthly ministry of Jesus, a period marked by Roman occupation and intense messianic expectation among the Jewish people.
35.passage: In Mark 1, Jesus begins His ministry by preaching, healing, and casting out demons. This verse highlights the importance of prayer in His life, even amidst intense activity.
35.culture: In the Jewish culture of the time, prayer was an essential practice, often performed in isolated places to avoid distractions and focus on God. The desert was also a symbol of divine encounter.
35.interpretation: This passage teaches us that even Jesus, the Son of God, took time to withdraw to pray. This underscores the importance of prayer in our own spiritual lives, as a means to connect with God and seek His direction.
35.commentaire: Mark 1:35 reminds us that prayer is fundamental for our spiritual growth. In a world filled with distractions, it is crucial to find moments of solitude to refocus on God. By imitating Jesus' example, we can prepare to face life's challenges with faith and assurance.

mots.sens: This verb means 'to seek' or 'to search for'. It implies an active quest, a search with a specific purpose. In the context of this verse, it emphasizes the urgency and determination of Simon's disciples to find Jesus, who had withdrawn to a desolate place to pray. Spiritually, this reminds us of the importance of seeking God's presence in our lives.

Simon, also known as Peter, is one of Jesus' closest disciples. His name means 'the one who listens'. As a leader among the disciples, his search for Jesus in this verse shows his desire to be in communion with the Master, which is essential for any believer aspiring to follow Christ and understand His will.

36.epoque: The historical context of this passage is set at the beginning of Jesus' ministry, when He begins to gather His disciples and teach in the region of Galilee. It is a time of great messianic expectation among the Jewish people.
36.passage: This verse is part of the beginning of Jesus' ministry, where He heals many people and preaches the Gospel. Mark chapter 1 highlights Jesus' authority and the impact of His teaching on those around Him.
36.culture: In the Jewish culture of the time, seeking a teacher or rabbi was an act of devotion and commitment. Disciples were often very dedicated to their master, seeking to follow him and learn from him.
36.interpretation: Simon and his companions' search reveals a deep desire to stay connected with Jesus, even when He withdraws to pray. This teaches us the importance of actively seeking God's presence in our lives, especially in moments of solitude and prayer.
36.commentaire: This verse reminds us that, just like Simon and his companions, we must be diligent in our quest for Christ's presence. In a world filled with distractions, it is essential to take the time to pray and seek God. May our hearts always be in pursuit of His closeness and direction.

mots.sens: This verb means 'to seek' or 'to search for' and implies an active quest, often with an intense desire. In the context of this verse, it emphasizes the urgency and determination of the people to find Jesus, who is perceived as the source of healing and hope. Spiritually, this can remind us of the importance of seeking the Lord with all our heart, for those who sincerely seek Him will find Him.

This term means 'all' and emphasizes the universality of the search for Jesus. It indicates that the interest in Jesus is not limited to a specific group but extends to all who witness His miracles and teaching. Theologically, this reminds us that Christ's call is for everyone, without distinction, and that each person is invited to know Him.

37.epoque: The historical context of this passage is set at the beginning of Jesus' ministry in the region of Galilee, where He begins to teach and perform miracles, thus attracting the attention of the crowds.
37.passage: In Mark 1, Jesus has just healed many sick people and cast out demons, causing great excitement among the inhabitants. This verse shows how people are in search of Jesus, illustrating the impact of His ministry on the community.
37.culture: The Jewish culture of the time valued teachers and healers, and Jesus' reputation was spreading rapidly. People were often in search of physical and spiritual healing, seeking answers to their suffering.
37.interpretation: This verse reveals the importance of the crowds' search for Jesus, highlighting their desperate need for Him. It teaches us that spiritual quest is essential and that Jesus is the one who satisfies our deepest needs.
37.commentaire: This passage encourages us to be like those who seek Jesus fervently. In our daily lives, we must also seek His presence and intervention in our struggles. By recognizing our need for Him, we can experience His power and grace, just as those who sought Him in the past.

mots.sens: This verb means 'to preach' or 'to prophesy'. It evokes the idea of conveying a divine message, often with a sense of urgency and authority. In the context of Mark 1:38, it underscores Jesus' mission to proclaim the kingdom of God, highlighting His role as Messiah and bearer of the good news. Spiritually, this reminds us of the importance of sharing the Gospel and being active witnesses of our faith.

This term means 'will' or 'intention'. It refers to the determination to act according to a divine plan. In this verse, Jesus clearly expresses His will to go preach in other towns, revealing His commitment to His mission. Theologically, this teaches us that our own will must be aligned with God's in our daily lives.

This verb means 'to come' or 'to go'. It is often used to describe physical movement, but in the context of this passage, it also symbolizes spiritual movement and Jesus' mission. It emphasizes the idea that Christ's mission is dynamic and not limited to a single place. It reminds us that we are called to go to others to share God's love.

38.epoque: The passage is set at the beginning of Jesus' ministry, in a context where He begins to attract the attention of the crowds in Galilee, a region marked by social and religious tensions.
38.passage: In Mark 1, Jesus has already healed many sick people and cast out demons. This verse shows a turning point where He decides to move to preach in other villages, highlighting the importance of His evangelistic mission.
38.culture: The Jewish culture of the time valued preaching and teaching in synagogues, but Jesus expands this scope by moving to less frequented places, thus showing that God's message is for everyone, not just the religious.
38.interpretation: This verse highlights Jesus' determination to fulfill His mission. By choosing to go to other towns, He demonstrates that the message of the kingdom of God must be spread widely, without being limited to a single place or group of people.
38.commentaire: Mark 1:38 reminds us that our mission as Christians is to go to others to share the good news of Jesus. Like Jesus, we must be sensitive to God's call and ready to move, physically or spiritually, to reach those who have not yet heard His message. This challenges us to reflect on our own commitment to evangelism and our willingness to go where God sends us.

mots.sens: This verb means 'to preach' or 'to announce publicly.' It evokes the idea of an authoritative proclamation, often associated with the dissemination of a divine message. In the context of Mark 1:39, it emphasizes the importance of Jesus' mission as the Messiah, whose message of salvation is intended to be heard by all. The theological significance of this word reminds us that the preaching of the Gospel is essential for the faith and spiritual transformation of believers.

This term refers to a 'synagogue,' a gathering place for prayer and the study of Scriptures. Historically, synagogues were community centers where Jews gathered for worship and learning. In this verse, it shows that Jesus first addresses his people, highlighting the importance of community in faith. Spiritually, it reminds us that collective worship and teaching are fundamental for spiritual growth.

This word translates to 'demon,' representing spiritual entities opposed to God. In the biblical context, demons are often associated with human suffering and oppression. The expulsion of demons by Jesus demonstrates his authority over the forces of evil and his role as Savior. Theologically, this underscores Christ's power over sin and suffering, offering hope of liberation to those who believe in him.

39.epoque: This passage is set at the beginning of Jesus' public ministry, in the 1st century, within the context of Roman-occupied Palestine. It is a period marked by strong messianic expectations among the Jewish people.
39.passage: In Mark 1, Jesus begins his ministry by preaching and healing, establishing his divine authority. This verse highlights the extension of his ministry throughout Galilee, marking an active phase of his redemptive work.
39.culture: The synagogue was a central place in Jewish life, serving both as a place of worship and religious education. The practice of preaching in these places shows the importance of teaching the law and the prophets in Jewish culture.
39.interpretation: This verse highlights Jesus' mission to preach the Gospel and to free the oppressed. By casting out demons, he demonstrates his authority over evil and invites believers to seek freedom and healing in him.
39.commentaire: Mark 1:39 reminds us that Jesus' mission is to touch lives through word and action. As disciples, we are called to follow his example by proclaiming the Gospel and bringing hope to the oppressed. This passage encourages us to be instruments of liberation and healing in our own community.

mots.sens: The term 'λέπρα' refers to leprosy, a serious and contagious skin disease, often associated with impurity in Jewish culture. In the biblical context, leprosy symbolizes not only physical suffering but also social and spiritual separation from the community. The healing of leprosy is therefore a powerful metaphor for purification and reconciliation with God.

The word 'θέλω' means 'to want' or 'to desire.' In this verse, it emphasizes the divine will and Jesus' ability to heal. This word evokes the sovereignty of Christ, who can choose to act according to his will, and highlights the importance of faith and submission to God's will in our quest for healing and purification.

The term 'προσερχομαι' means 'to approach' or 'to come to.' In this context, it indicates the act of coming close to Jesus with humility and supplication. This underscores the importance of a personal and sincere approach to Christ, who is the only one capable of purifying us from our sins and sufferings.

40.epoque: In Jesus' time, leprosy was considered a shameful disease, leading to the social isolation of the sick. Lepers were often excluded from the community, which heightened their physical and psychological suffering.
40.passage: This passage is set at the beginning of Jesus' ministry, where he begins to reveal his authority over diseases and demons. Mark 1 highlights the miracles of Jesus and his compassion for those who suffer.
40.culture: In Jewish culture, ritual purity was essential, and leprosy represented an impurity that prevented access to worship. The healing of a leper was therefore not only a physical restoration but also a reintegration into the religious community.
40.interpretation: This verse shows the faith of the leper who, despite his marginalized status, approaches Jesus with confidence in his ability to heal. It also illustrates Jesus' willingness to purify those who come to him, regardless of their past or condition.
40.commentaire: This passage teaches us the importance of approaching Jesus with faith and humility, recognizing our need for purification. Like the leper, we are called to kneel before Christ, knowing that he has the power to transform our lives. Spiritual and physical healing is always possible by his will, and we must be ready to receive his grace.

mots.sens: This verb means 'to have compassion' and evokes a deep emotion that comes from the bowels. It is a term that indicates an intense reaction to the suffering of others, highlighting Jesus' empathetic nature. In this verse, it shows that Jesus' compassion is not merely an emotion but a call to action to bring healing and redemption.

This word means 'pure' or 'holy.' In the context of the healing of leprosy, it evokes the idea of restoration to a state of purity, both physical and spiritual. The purification of leprosy symbolizes Jesus' ability to cleanse not only physical ailments but also sins, thus offering a new life.

This verb means 'to have' or 'to hold.' In the context of this verse, it is used to express Jesus' will, affirming his authority over disease. This emphasizes that the divine will is always in favor of healing and restoration, reinforcing the message of God's love and mercy.

41.epoque: This passage is set at the beginning of Jesus' ministry, in a context where diseases and sufferings were often seen as consequences of sin or impurity. The Jewish society of the time had strict laws regarding ritual purity, particularly concerning lepers.
41.passage: In this chapter, Jesus begins to preach, heal the sick, and free the oppressed. The account of the healing of the leper highlights Jesus' compassion and his power over diseases, while illustrating his desire to restore those who are rejected by society.
41.culture: In Jewish culture, lepers were often excluded from the community and considered impure. Mosaic law stipulated strict rituals for purification, and contact with a leper was taboo. Jesus, by touching the leper, defies these social and religious norms.
41.interpretation: This verse illustrates the merciful nature of Jesus, who is moved by human suffering and acts with authority to bring healing. It also shows that Jesus' purity and holiness are not contaminated by contact with impurity, but rather bring healing and restoration.
41.commentaire: This passage reminds us that compassion should be at the heart of our ministry and interactions with others. As disciples of Christ, we are called to touch those who suffer, to listen to them, and to bring them the hope of healing. Jesus teaches us that, even in a world that stigmatizes and rejects, we have the power to spread love and mercy.

mots.sens: The term 'λεπρός' refers to a person afflicted with leprosy, a skin disease considered impure in Jewish culture. This condition symbolizes not only physical suffering but also social and spiritual separation. In the biblical context, leprosy is often used to illustrate sin and the need for purification, thus highlighting the theological significance of Jesus' healing as an act of redemption and restoration.

The verb 'ἀφήκεν' means 'to leave' or 'to depart,' implying an immediate and complete action. In this verse, it emphasizes that the leprosy left the man instantly upon contact with Jesus, illustrating Christ's divine authority over disease. It also evokes the notion of liberation from sin and suffering, showing that Jesus has the power to radically transform the lives of those who approach Him.

The word 'καθαρός' means 'pure' or 'clean,' and in the context of healing, it represents the complete restoration of the individual. This purification goes beyond physical healing, touching the soul and social status of the person. Spiritually, it illustrates Jesus' ability to cleanse and restore those who are spiritually defiled by sin, offering a new life in Him.

42.epoque: The passage is set at the beginning of Jesus' ministry, in a context where leprosy was feared and led to the social isolation of the afflicted. The Mosaic laws stipulated strict rules regarding lepers, considering them impure.
42.passage: This verse is part of a larger narrative where Jesus begins to manifest His authority through miracles, establishing His divine identity. It shows how Jesus responds to human suffering with compassion and power.
42.culture: In the Jewish culture of the time, lepers were excluded from the community and religious life, which intensified their suffering. Jesus' healing of a leper is therefore a revolutionary act that challenges social and religious norms.
42.interpretation: The immediate healing of the man with leprosy symbolizes Jesus' power over sin and disease. It demonstrates that Jesus is capable of restoring not only physical health but also the relationship with God, making the believer pure and acceptable before Him.
42.commentaire: This verse reminds us that Jesus is the one who purifies and restores. In our lives, we can approach Him with our own 'leprosies,' whether physical, emotional, or spiritual, and experience His healing power. This encourages us to have faith in His ability to transform our lives and restore us in our relationship with God.

mots.sens: This verb means 'to command' or 'to insistently recommend.' It evokes a serious and authoritative instruction, often used in a context where obedience is expected. In this verse, it emphasizes the importance of Jesus' directive, which is not merely a suggestion but involves a spiritual responsibility for the one who has been healed.

This term means 'to present' or 'to recommend.' It carries a connotation of putting forward, often in a context of testimony or validation. In the context of this verse, it indicates that Jesus wants the healed man to testify about his experience, but with a certain reserve, in order to preserve the integrity of His ministry.

43.epoque: In the first century, Palestine was under Roman rule, with a strong Jewish religious influence. Jesus' miracles attracted attention but also sparked tensions with religious and political authorities.
43.passage: This verse is situated at the beginning of Jesus' ministry, after He has healed a leper. This chapter highlights Jesus' power and authority over disease and purification while introducing the challenges of His ministry.
43.culture: In Jewish culture, leprosy was considered a serious impurity, and lepers were excluded from the community. Jesus' healing of a leper is therefore a radical act that questions the social and religious norms of the time.
43.interpretation: By sending the leper away with strict recommendations, Jesus emphasizes the importance of discretion and humility in testimony. He teaches that spiritual and physical healing must be accompanied by an understanding of the divine mission and obedience to His instructions.
43.commentaire: This verse reminds us that our encounter with Jesus must be followed by an active and responsible response. As believers, we are called to testify to our faith with wisdom and discernment, respecting God's instructions. Spiritual healing involves not only personal transformation but also a commitment to live according to divine precepts.

mots.sens: This term refers to a priest, a person consecrated to the service of God in worship. In the Jewish context, the priest plays an essential role in intercession and mediation between God and the people. Spiritually, this word underscores the importance of spiritual authority and ritual purification in the relationship with God.

This word means purification or cleansing, often in relation to religious rites. It evokes the idea of making something pure or acceptable before God. In the context of this verse, it underscores the necessity of spiritual and physical purification to be in communion with God and the community.

This term means testimony or evidence, and it implies a declaration of truth. In this verse, it indicates that the action of the healed man will serve as a testimony to the power of Jesus. Theologically, this highlights the importance of bearing witness to God's grace in our lives.

44.epoque: This passage is set at the beginning of Jesus' ministry, in a context where the Mosaic law and Jewish religious practices were central to the life of the people of Israel.
44.passage: In this chapter, Jesus begins to teach and heal, demonstrating His divine authority. This verse illustrates how Jesus, while having the power to heal, respects Jewish laws and traditions.
44.culture: In Jewish culture, ritual purification was essential to maintain holiness and acceptance before God. The testimony to the priest was an act of obedience to the Mosaic law.
44.interpretation: This verse shows that physical healing must be followed by a spiritual and communal approach. Jesus asks the healed man to conform to the prescriptions of the law to testify to God's work in his life.
44.commentaire: This passage reminds us of the importance of obedience to God's word and the rites of purification. By testifying to our healing and transformation, we glorify God and encourage others to seek the same grace. We are called to live our faith authentically, respecting the traditions that bring us closer to God.

mots.sens: This verb means 'to preach' or 'to announce publicly.' In the context of this verse, it emphasizes the action of the healed man who, through his testimony, spreads the fame of Jesus. The root of the word evokes an authorized proclamation, highlighting the importance of communicating the message of the Gospel. Spiritually, this reminds us that our testimony can influence the perception of Christ in our surroundings.

This term refers to a 'field' or an 'open place,' often used to describe outdoor spaces. In this passage, it refers to the deserted places where Jesus withdraws. This evokes a separation from the crowds, underscoring the need for solitude for prayer and communion with the Father. Theologically, this reminds us that even Jesus, though He is the Son of God, needed moments of withdrawal to be spiritually replenished.

This verb means 'to increase' or 'to multiply.' In the context of this verse, it describes how the fame of Jesus grows because of the testimonies of healing. This highlights the power of personal testimony in the spread of faith. Spiritually, it teaches us that our commitment to share what God has done in our lives can draw others to Christ.

45.epoque: This passage is set at the beginning of Jesus' ministry, during a time when Palestine was under Roman rule and messianic expectations were high among the Jewish people.
45.passage: In Mark 1, Jesus begins His public ministry by preaching the Gospel and performing miracles. This verse illustrates the people's reaction to His works, showing how the healing of a leper led to a great influx towards Him.
45.culture: At that time, leprosy was a feared disease, leading to the social isolation of the sick. The healing of a leper was therefore seen as an act of great divine power, eliciting admiration and curiosity from the crowds.
45.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the impact of testimony on the dissemination of Jesus' message. The healed man, by sharing his experience, contributes to the fame of Jesus, but this also has consequences for Jesus' ability to move freely. Spiritually, this teaches us that our faith and testimony can have significant repercussions on our environment.
45.commentaire: This passage reminds us of the importance of sharing our faith testimony. Like this healed man, we are called to proclaim what God has done for us, even if it may complicate our lives at times. Furthermore, it invites us to seek moments of solitude with God to renew our strength and vision, so that we may better serve those who come to us.
